questions.q: Which e-mail protocol keeps messages on the server so that the same mailbox stays in sync across a phone, tablet and laptop?
questions.solution: IMAP stores mail on the server and synchronises state across devices. POP3 traditionally downloads and removes mail (single-device model), SMTP sends, FTP moves files.

questions.q: Mail merge in MS Word is used to:
options: Merge two documents into one file
Create personalised copies of a document for many recipients
questions.solution: Mail merge generates letters/labels/envelopes/e-mails where a common main document is personalised from a data source - one template, many recipients.
questions.shortcut: 'Same letter, many names' = mail merge; the trap options play on the word 'merge'.

questions.q: At which layer of the OSI model does a switch primarily operate?
questions.solution: Switches forward frames using MAC (hardware) addresses, which belong to the Data Link layer (2). Routers use IP at layer 3.
questions.shortcut: MAC-address device = layer 2; IP device = layer 3.

questions.q: Which shortcut sets double line spacing in MS Word?
questions.solution: Ctrl+2 gives double spacing, Ctrl+1 single spacing and Ctrl+5 1.5 spacing. Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog.
questions.shortcut: The digit is the spacing; 5 means 1.5.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Restaurant = **rest-au-rant**: the 'au' sits between rest and rant. Restaraunt reverses to 'ar'; Restauraunt adds a phantom u.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

She said that she had seen him the day before.
options: She said, "I had seen him yesterday."
She said, "I have seen him yesterday."
She said, "I saw him the previous day."
questions.solution: 'the day before' → **yesterday**; past perfect → **simple past** (saw) when the time anchor is restored; she → I, him stays. B keeps 'had seen' inside quotes; C pairs present perfect with yesterday (impossible); D leaves reported time words in a quote.
questions.shortcut: Reverse ladder: had + V3 → V2 when the anchor returns as yesterday.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

___ it rained heavily throughout the day, the final match was not ___.
questions.solution: The clauses contrast (rain vs the match happening) → concession: **Although** — this eliminates both 'Because' pairs. A match that is not played is **called off**; *called on* visits, *called up* telephones. Only the first pair completes both halves.
questions.shortcut: Anchor the connective (contrast → Although), then match the phrasal to the meaning.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

All the ___ items — pens, registers and markers — were locked in the storeroom.
questions.solution: Pens, registers and markers are writing materials: **stationery**. *Stationary* means not moving — the items may be stationary too, but the apposition with the list pins the meaning to the writing-materials word.
questions.shortcut: Context picture: pens and registers → stationery.

questions.q: With reference to NITI Aayog, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: It was set up in 2014 as the successor to the Finance Commission
It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament
It continues the Five Year Plan process
It was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission
questions.solution: NITI Aayog was created by a **Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015**, replacing the Planning Commission (1950) after the 12th Plan ended. It is neither constitutional nor statutory, and it does not allocate Plan funds.
questions.shortcut: Statutory test fails → only the '1 Jan 2015 replacement' statement can be true.

questions.q: Who renounced his knighthood in protest against the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** of 1919?
questions.solution: **Rabindranath Tagore** gave up the knighthood conferred on him in 1915 by writing to the Viceroy (Lord Chelmsford) in May 1919. Gandhi later returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal.
questions.shortcut: Only a 'Sir' could renounce a knighthood → Sir Rabindranath.

questions.q: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which becomes effective from 1 April 2026, is notable for:
options: introducing a single 'tax year' and replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961
raising the basic exemption limit to ₹7 lakh
questions.solution: The Income-tax Act, 2025 consolidates the 1961 Act into **536 sections across 23 chapters** and replaces the previous-year/assessment-year pair with one **'tax year'** (first applicable to income of FY 2026-27). Rates and slabs are essentially unchanged; GST law is untouched.
questions.shortcut: Keyword of the new Act = 'tax year' — nothing about GST or new slabs.

questions.q: Which committee recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj system consisting of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat?
questions.solution: The **Ashok Mehta Committee (1977)** suggested a **two-tier** scheme — Zila Parishad at the district and Mandal Panchayat (cluster of villages) below it. Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) had recommended **three tiers**, G.V.K. Rao (1985) wanted the district as the planning unit, and L.M. Singhvi (1986) sought constitutional status.
questions.shortcut: Tier count mnemonic: Balwant-3, Ashok-2 ('B-A = 3-2'), Rao-district, Singhvi-Constitution.

questions.q: Two pipes fill a tank in 8 hours and 12 hours, while a third pipe empties the full tank in 6 hours. With all three open, the empty tank is filled in:
A six-digit number is formed by writing a three-digit number twice (for example 257257). Such a number is always divisible by:
questions.solution: $abcabc = abc \times 1000 + abc = abc \times 1001$ and $1001 = 7 \times 11 \times 13$. So it is always divisible by 7, 11 and 13.

questions.q: The shadow of a pole is $\sqrt{3}$ times the height of the pole. The angle of elevation of the sun is:
questions.solution: $\tan\theta=\frac{h}{\sqrt3\,h}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow\theta=30^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: Shadow $\sqrt3\times$ height is the signature of 30° ($d=\sqrt3h$). Trap: 60° inverts the ratio.

questions.q: The average of 30 results was 20. It was later found that a result of 24 had been wrongly recorded as 21. The corrected average is:
questions.solution: Shortfall $=24-21=3$. Corrected mean $=\frac{600+3}{30}=20.1$.
questions.shortcut: Add the error to the total and re-divide: $\frac{603}{30}=20.1$.

questions.q: Find the odd pair out: **Author : Book, Poet : Poem, Sculptor : Statue, Painter : Canvas**
questions.solution: Author-book, poet-poem and sculptor-statue are **creator-creation** pairs. A canvas is the painter's **surface**, not his creation — the painting is → **Painter : Canvas**.
questions.shortcut: Pair lists: write the majority relation once, then tick/cross each pair against it.
questions.pattern: pair odd one out — relation break

questions.q: **Asha walks 6 m towards East, turns right and walks 8 m.** How far is she from the starting point?
questions.solution: Components (6, 8) = 2 × (3, 4) → distance = 2 × 5 = **10 m**. (14 m is the path walked.)
questions.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish

questions.q: In a queue, **A is 9th from the front and B is 21st from the front.** Who stands **exactly in the middle** of A and B (in position, not count)?
questions.solution: Middle position = (9 + 21) ÷ 2 = **15th from the front**. (The count of people between them is 11 — different question.)
